summary: A grazing table is the table itself built up with food over paper, not a board. Caterers suggest about 6 ft for 20 to 30 guests, 8 to 12 ft for 40 to 60 (both sides reachable), 12 to 16 ft for 75 to 100, and splitting into 2 or 3 stations past about 150 guests. A calculator rule of thumb is about 1 ft of length per 10 guests, 5 to 6 oz of food per person for light grazing. A standard 30 in wide, 30 in high folding table is the usual base (8 ft is 2.44 m). Building a big one takes 2 to 3 hours on site, so give the caterer room access, and keep it in shade in summer heat.
